answer.answer: Straylight is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth. The 2026-07-26 current-status note controls; the older green checkpoint is historical and explicitly superseded by production-sized findings. The approved direction is a changed-file versioning model with rebuildable derived state and precise checkpoints, while preserving coherent hydration and compact retrieval packets.

claims.value: Projects/Straylight current status.md, updated 2026-07-26T12:00:00-07:00, is the controlling current implementation truth and says the architecture is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x corpus growth. Projects/Straylight stale checkpoint.md, recorded 2026-07-23T18:00:00-07:00, is historical evidence only: its passing retrieval test corpus, healthy `/ready` configuration, and proposal to open the owner alpha immediately predate the production-sized timeout and full-manifest-copy findings and must not override the newer note.

Broad `memory.open` and lexical retrieval are slow and can hit the 30-second database timeout. Because retrieval lanes share one transaction, a later lane failure can also discard an earlier lane’s successful result. Connection, authentication, and exact-path reads work, but these production retrieval behaviors prevent dependable owner readiness at 10x corpus growth.

Normal writes copy a full corpus membership manifest. With about 64,000 active records and 9.6 million estimated source tokens already in the owner corpus, this full-manifest copying is the identified write-amplification mechanism and contributes to the conclusion that the current architecture is not ready for dependable owner use at 10x growth.

The approved direction—not a verified completed migration—is to make current Markdown files the workspace truth, version only changed files, make indexes and derived views rebuildable, and checkpoint with exact path, version, and hash references plus changes since a workspace generation, while retaining coherent source hydration and compact retrieval packets.
